A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Measuring Uncertainty Calibration and contain readable main text, equations, five figures, Table 1 and appendices A–I. The material supports reliable comparison, including relocated content.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original classifier-perturbation experiments, synthetic and real-data calibration-bound comparisons, and empirical convergence rates. Appendix H adds calibration-function reconstruction results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Figures 2–4 and Table 1, together with the reconstruction results in Appendix H and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The TV-denoising estimator, score perturbation, Nadaraya–Watson surrogate and perturbation-aware training loss remain unchanged. Appendix E explains existing bandwidth and bucketing choices without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four synthetic calibration functions and seven real datasets: IMDb, Spam Detection, binary CIFAR-10, Amazon Polarity, Civil Comments, Phishing and Yelp Polarity. Task definitions are unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains NW, TV, Lip+Bkt and ECE; Figure 4 retains NW, TV and Lip+Bkt. Figure 2 retains the same perturbed-versus-unperturbed classifier comparisons.

E3.justification: The metrics, model families, dataset splits, sample counts, perturbation settings, cross-fitting and validation subsampling are unchanged. Appendix E newly clarifies implementation choices without reporting a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The perturbation-size sensitivity study in Figure 2 and the reconstruction analysis in Appendix H/Figure 5 are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 64 repeats and mean performance, with the same explanation for omitting confidence bars from Figure 3. No changes to run counts, uncertainty reporting or significance procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 retain identical plotted results. Table 1 retains empirical-rate ranges of [-0.406, -0.213] for NW, [-0.423, -0.164] for TV and [-0.574, -0.346] for Lip+Bkt. The accompanying findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 corrects Lemma 2's second squared summand from ((j-|T|)/|T|)^2 to (j/|T|)^2. Appendix B.5 adds when Lemma 5's boundary term can be omitted, and Appendix E derives the existing bandwidth rule. Section 4 also replaces n with |T|, although Proposition 1 thereby explicitly normalizes a validation-set sum by training-set size.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same two contributions: certified calibration bounds under bounded variation, and perturbation-enabled bounds under bounded derivatives. Their claimed scope and distribution-free, non-asymptotic character remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly qualifies the bandwidth proxy as using locally uniform score-density approximations and ignoring boundary effects. These clarify the heuristic's justification. The empirical interpretations and Section 11 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement replaces a promise to release code upon acceptance with reported availability and a repository link. Appendix E adds details about equal-width shifted bins and the approximations behind the existing bandwidth constants and optimization.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning remain unchanged. Maalej et al. (2025) moves between related-work paragraphs, while the Phishing reference changes attribution from aisuko to Li (2024) but retains the same dataset title and URL.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language and capitalization corrections, updates author names and the publication header, moves a related-work sentence, and expands Appendix E's explanations. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from the bottom to the top of page 2, and Figure 5 moves from page 27 to page 28. Appendix text and equations reflow, while figure content and Table 1's structure remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The repaired Lemma 2 calculation, clearer bandwidth derivation and reported source-code access provide a modest gain in auditability and reproducibility. The empirical evidence and central contributions remain unchanged. Proposition 1's newly explicit training-size denominator for a validation sum remains inconsistent with its averaging argument for unequal splits, limiting the improvement in mathematical reliability.
